question: Which correctly describes a 'foundry' in the semiconductor industry?
choices: A company specializing in contract manufacturing of semiconductors designed by other companies
A company with no factories that specializes in semiconductor design and sales
A company specializing in selling parts for semiconductor manufacturing equipment
explanation: A foundry is a company (or business) that manufactures wafers under contract from circuit data designed by its customers. TSMC, founded in 1987, established the pure-play foundry model. Sharing costly leading-edge fabs among many customers spread the division of labor with fabless companies. Companies that own no fabs and focus on design and sales are fabless, and those selling equipment parts belong to the tool supply chain.

question: Which correctly describes a 'fabless' company?
choices: A company that handles everything from design to manufacturing and sales in-house
A company that has no manufacturing plants of its own and specializes in design and sales
A company that takes on only back-end semiconductor processes on contract
explanation: Fabless means having no fab (manufacturing plant). These companies concentrate on design and sales, outsourcing manufacturing to foundries and assembly and test to OSATs. With no need for huge plant investments, even young companies can bring leading-edge products to market, and many major GPU and smartphone SoC vendors operate this way. Companies doing everything from design to manufacturing are IDMs, and those taking on back-end work are OSATs.

question: Which best describes 'Moore's law'?
choices: Clock frequency increases tenfold every 18 months
The number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles every fixed period (about two years)
explanation: Moore's law is the empirical observation that the number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles at regular intervals. Gordon Moore proposed annual doubling in 1965 and revised it to about every two years in 1975. It is not a law of physics but has served as the industry's development target. It does not say prices halve every year or frequency rises tenfold in 18 months. The pace of doubling is said to have slowed recently.

question: Which correctly describes companies called OSATs?
choices: Companies that take on back-end processes such as semiconductor assembly and test on contract
explanation: An OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) company provides back-end services, assembling (packaging) and testing chips. Major OSATs are concentrated in Taiwan, China and Southeast Asia, with strengths in labor and geographically dispersed sites. Together with foundries for front-end work and fabless design houses, they form the industry's division of labor. As advanced packaging grows in importance, foundries themselves increasingly do back-end work.

question: In the semiconductor market, what is the phenomenon called in which booms and busts repeat periodically due to the balance of supply and demand?
explanation: The silicon cycle is the recurring boom and bust in which capacity investment made during demand growth leads to oversupply a few years later, followed by price declines, investment cuts and renewed shortages. Because a fab takes about two years from construction to volume production, investment decisions lag demand changes; the cycle has traditionally been about four years. Moore's law and Dennard scaling are technology rules of thumb.

question: Which type of semiconductor company handles everything from design through front-end and back-end manufacturing to sales in-house?
explanation: An IDM (integrated device manufacturer) handles design, manufacturing and sales in-house. Proximity between design and process teams makes it easier to co-optimize process and product, but it demands huge fab investments. IDMs are common in memory, power and analog semiconductors, where manufacturing technology itself differentiates the product. Fabless firms own no fabs, and OSATs perform back-end services.

question: Which correctly describes Dennard scaling?
choices: The number of transistors doubles about every two years
Shrinking transistor dimensions and supply voltage by the same ratio allows higher speed and integration while keeping power density constant
The semiconductor market repeats booms and busts on a cycle of about four years
explanation: Dennard scaling, described by Robert Dennard and colleagues in 1974, states that shrinking transistor dimensions and voltage by the same factor k keeps power per unit area constant while making devices faster and smaller. In the mid-2000s, rising leakage made it hard to lower threshold and supply voltages, and scaling no longer followed this rule. That is why clock frequency growth stalled and the industry shifted to multicore.

question: Which appropriately describes generation names (node names) of advanced processes such as the '3 nm generation'?
choices: They mean the gate length is exactly 3 nm
They mean the wafer thickness is 3 nm
In recent years, they have become generation labels that do not necessarily match physical dimensions such as actual gate length
explanation: Process names once roughly matched dimensions such as gate length, but since the introduction of FinFETs and other changes, recent node names no longer correspond directly to physical dimensions and instead denote improvements in performance and density. Even at the "3 nm" node, the transistor pitch is over 40 nm. The same name can mean different densities at different companies, so metrics such as transistor density are used for comparison.

question: What is the scheme called in which a foundry puts designs from several customers on one wafer (one mask set) for prototyping?
explanation: An MPW (multi-project wafer) combines several designs on one mask set and wafer run, sharing mask and fabrication costs among participants; it is also called a shuttle, like a shared bus. Since advanced-node mask sets can cost tens of millions of dollars, universities and startups use MPWs for low-cost prototyping. Each participant gets only a few chips, so it serves prototyping and evaluation, not volume production. OSAT and IDM are business models.

question: Which appropriately describes investment in advanced semiconductor fabs?
choices: A cutting-edge fab can be built with a small investment (a few hundred million yen)
Manufacturing equipment such as exposure tools is expensive, and building an advanced fab can require investment on the scale of trillions of yen
Production relies mainly on manual labor with almost no manufacturing equipment
explanation: Fabrication equipment is extremely expensive, with a single leading-edge EUV scanner costing hundreds of millions of dollars, and tools account for most of a fab's construction cost. Building an advanced fab can require investment on the scale of tens of billions of dollars, driving concentration of manufacturing at foundries and government subsidy programs. A few million dollars would not buy even one leading-edge tool, and nanometer-scale processing cannot be done by hand.

question: What is an LSI called that integrates functions a system needs, such as a CPU, GPU, memory controller and communications, on a single chip?
explanation: An SoC integrates most of a system's functions on a single chip; smartphone processors are the classic example. Eliminating chip-to-chip wiring reduces part count and makes systems smaller, faster and lower-power. On the other hand, larger dies yield worse, and circuits requiring different processes are hard to combine. It is distinguished from an SiP, which houses multiple chips in one package. Commodity DRAM is a standalone memory product.

question: What is an LSI called that is custom-designed for a specific application or customer?
explanation: An ASIC (application specific integrated circuit) is designed specifically for a particular product or application. Optimized for just the needed functions, it excels in performance and power, but high development costs including masks and months of development time mean it is used where sufficient volume is expected. Reprogrammable FPGAs suit low volumes and prototypes, and commodity memory serves many applications alike.

question: Which category of semiconductor products, such as diodes, single transistors and power MOSFETs, performs a single function on its own?
explanation: Discrete semiconductors are products that function as a single device, such as diodes, transistors, thyristors, power MOSFETs and IGBTs. They are distinguished from integrated circuits (ICs), which integrate many devices on one chip. Power devices handling high current or voltage are often supplied as discretes or modules for thermal and voltage reasons, and many are made on mature processes. Logic and memory ICs are integrated circuits.

question: Which correctly distinguishes the 'front end' and 'back end' of semiconductor manufacturing?
choices: The front end is design, and the back end is manufacturing
The front end builds circuits on the wafer, and the back end cuts out chips and assembles and tests them
The front end is testing, and the back end is wafer manufacturing
explanation: The front end builds circuits on the wafer by repeating deposition, lithography, etching, ion implantation and other steps. The back end packages chips diced from the wafer, tests them and ships them. Design is a separate stage before manufacturing. As advanced packaging that performs redistribution or die stacking at the wafer level grows in importance, the boundary between the two is blurring.

question: What is the direction called that raises value not only by increasing integration through scaling but also by combining diverse functions such as sensors, power, analog and advanced packaging?
explanation: More than Moore refers to adding function and value through technologies other than scaling, such as sensors, MEMS, power, RF and advanced packaging, in contrast to More Moore, which pursues scaling. These products do not necessarily need leading-edge geometries and can create value on mature processes. Their importance grows with diverse applications such as IoT and automotive. Dennard scaling and the silicon cycle are different concepts.

question: Which is an appropriate example of a field that has strongly boosted semiconductor demand in recent years?
explanation: The spread of generative AI is rapidly expanding demand for data-center GPUs and AI accelerators, along with the HBM paired with them. AI training requires massive computation and memory bandwidth, and a single data center may house tens of thousands of GPUs or more. Vehicle electrification and added functionality, industrial equipment and IoT also drive semiconductor demand. Floppy disks and vacuum-tube radios are products of the past.

question: Which appropriately describes cutting-edge EUV exposure tools?
choices: Many companies supply them cheaply, and they are easy to obtain
Very few companies can supply them, and they are central to manufacturing advanced semiconductors
They are not used to manufacture advanced semiconductors
explanation: EUV scanners combine a plasma light source created by firing lasers at tin droplets, multilayer mirrors with about 70% reflectivity, and high-vacuum technology; in practice only ASML in the Netherlands supplies production tools. Each costs hundreds of millions of dollars and is indispensable for leading-edge logic and memory. Their components come from specialist suppliers worldwide, and the tools are subject to export controls.

question: Which is an appropriate main reason governments are providing large-scale support to the semiconductor industry?
choices: Because demand for semiconductors has disappeared
Because semiconductors have become strategic goods essential to the economy and national security, and domestic supply chains need strengthening
explanation: Semiconductors are essential to every industry and to defense, yet leading-edge manufacturing is concentrated in a few regions, raising awareness of supply-disruption risk; the chip shortages of the early 2020s drove this home. The US CHIPS Act and programs in Japan, Europe and South Korea therefore provide large-scale support for attracting fabs and funding R&D. Demand has not vanished, and the aim is not to shrink the industry.

question: Which appropriately describes the role scaling has played in semiconductor cost?
choices: It has fit more transistors in the same area, lowering the cost per transistor
It has lowered manufacturing cost per wafer
It has reduced the number of transistors per chip
explanation: Scaling has raised manufacturing cost per wafer, but even more transistors fit on each wafer, so cost per transistor has fallen. That is why chips at the same price have gained functionality each generation. Recently, steep wafer price increases at advanced nodes are said to have slowed the decline in cost per transistor. Transistors per chip have increased, not decreased.

question: Which industry body develops standards for DRAM such as DDR?
explanation: JEDEC, dating from 1958, is the semiconductor standards body that defines DRAM standards such as DDR, LPDDR, GDDR and HBM, as well as package and reliability test standards. Common standards let memory and processors from different vendors work together and foster market competition. ISO is the International Organization for Standardization, and SEMI is the industry association handling standards for equipment and materials.

question: Which region is known for an especially heavy concentration of contract (foundry) manufacturing of advanced logic semiconductors?
explanation: Contract manufacturing of leading-edge logic is heavily concentrated in Taiwanese companies, which are said to produce most of the world's output at the most advanced nodes. This concentration is viewed as a supply risk from earthquakes and geopolitical tension, motivating efforts in the US, Japan and Europe to attract fabs. Northern Europe and South America have no large leading-edge foundries.

question: Which is commonly said to characterize the memory market?
choices: Prices tend to fluctuate greatly with the balance of supply and demand
explanation: DRAM and NAND flash are standardized products that are hard to differentiate, so prices swing widely with supply and demand, sometimes halving within a year. Capacity expansion during booms tends to cause oversupply in downturns, making memory makers' earnings highly volatile. Technically demanding products such as HBM, however, can be supplied by only a few companies and command high prices.

question: Which is an appropriate example of products designed by fabless companies?
explanation: Fabless companies design smartphone SoCs, GPUs, communication chips, networking chips and the like, outsourcing manufacturing to foundries and assembly and test to OSATs. Their value comes from circuit design and software, and many enjoy high profit margins. Silicon wafers are made by materials companies and scanners by equipment makers; they are not fabless products.

question: Which is an appropriate field in which Japan's semiconductor-related industry is said to have global strength?
choices: Manufacturing equipment and materials (wafers, resists, high-purity chemicals and gases, etc.)
explanation: Japan is home to many companies with high global shares in materials such as silicon wafers, photoresists and high-purity chemicals and gases, and in equipment for coating and developing, cleaning, deposition and inspection. Their strength comes from long accumulated materials expertise and experience meeting stringent quality demands, giving them an important place in the supply chain. Smartphone operating systems and GPU design are areas where mainly US companies lead.

question: Which is an appropriate example of an issue facing the semiconductor industry in recent years?
choices: Shortages of engineers and technicians accompanying the construction of new fabs
Technology development is no longer necessary
explanation: With new fabs being built around the world, securing process engineers, equipment engineers and skilled production technicians has become a major challenge. Even a completed fab cannot ramp without people to run the tools and raise yields. Governments, companies, universities and technical colleges are collaborating to develop talent. Neither demand nor the need for technology development has disappeared.

question: Which is closest to the approximate size of the global semiconductor market (annual revenue) in recent years?
choices: Several hundred billion to over one trillion dollars
explanation: The global semiconductor market reached several hundred billion dollars per year in the early 2020s. Demand for data-center AI chips and memory then surged, and the industry statistics organization WSTS forecasts it will far exceed one trillion dollars in 2026. At 150 yen to the dollar, one trillion dollars is about 150 trillion yen. The market has grown over the long term through repeated booms and busts. A few hundred million or hundreds of trillions of dollars are off by orders of magnitude.

question: Which is an appropriate reason the division of labor between foundries and fabless companies spread?
choices: Because investment in advanced fabs became huge, making it more efficient to separate design and manufacturing
explanation: Building a leading-edge fab requires enormous investment, and it became hard for one company's products to fill a fab. Consolidating manufacturing at specialized foundries lets many customers share equipment and keeps utilization high, while design companies focus on product development without owning fabs. This spread the division of labor, and some IDMs gave up their fabs to become fabless or fab-lite. Manufacturing has become harder, not easier.

question: Which is an appropriate reason the back end (packaging) has become more important in recent years?
choices: Because the back end is no longer needed
Because package cost has fallen to almost zero
Because chiplets and advanced packaging have become important means of raising system performance
explanation: As scaling alone struggles to raise performance, advanced packaging that densely interconnects multiple chips has become a way to boost performance and power efficiency. For AI chips, capacity for 2.5D packaging, which places HBM beside the processor and links them through a silicon interposer, now constrains product supply. The back end has neither become unnecessary nor free.

question: Which is an appropriate reason the amount of semiconductors in each car is increasing?
choices: Because electrification, driver assistance and information and communications functions have increased, using many more microcontrollers, power semiconductors, sensors and so on
Because electronics have disappeared from cars
explanation: Electric vehicles use power semiconductors in inverters that drive the motors, and driver-assistance systems need camera and radar sensors plus high-performance processors. Infotainment, connectivity and numerous electronic control units (ECUs) add more, so semiconductor content per vehicle has risen sharply. Automotive parts require long-term supply and high reliability, and many are made on mature processes.

question: What is a company called whose business model is licensing design assets (IP) such as CPUs to other companies for fees?
explanation: IP vendors develop design assets such as CPU cores and interface circuits and license them to chip companies, earning upfront license fees and per-unit royalties. Most smartphone processors use CPU cores licensed from IP vendors. Using IP lets chip companies cut development time and cost. Foundries provide manufacturing and OSATs back-end services.

question: Because semiconductors are basic components essential to all kinds of products, what metaphor has been used for them in Japan?
explanation: Because semiconductors are basic components used in every kind of product, from appliances and cars to communication equipment and computers, they have been called "the rice of industry" in Japan, likening them to the staple food. The phrase spread in the 1980s, when Japanese makers led the world in DRAM. Today they are also valued as strategic goods underpinning the economy and national security, sometimes described as "the brain of industry."
choiceNotes: Correct. It likens them to the staple food, rice.
This expression is not commonly used.
This expression is not commonly used.

question: In the memory semiconductor market, which two products account for most of the revenue?
explanation: Most memory revenue comes from DRAM, used as main memory in computers and smartphones, and NAND flash, used for SSDs and smartphone storage. Recently, HBM for AI, a form of DRAM, has grown revenue substantially. Both are prone to large price swings with supply and demand, and memory market conditions drive much of the ups and downs of the overall semiconductor market.
choiceNotes: These are now products with small markets.
Correct. DRAM and NAND are the core of the memory market.
SRAM is mainly embedded inside processors, and MRAM's market is still small.

question: Which company, headquartered in Taiwan, holds the largest share of the world's foundry (contract chip manufacturing) market?
explanation: TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company), founded in 1987, is a pure-play foundry and holds the largest share of the foundry market. Having no products of its own and never competing with customers earns their trust, and it manufactures leading-edge logic for many fabless companies. It has also built fabs in Japan (Kumamoto) and the US. ASML makes lithography tools and Synopsys EDA software.
choiceNotes: ASML is a Dutch maker of lithography systems.
Synopsys is a US EDA tool company.
Correct. It is the world's largest foundry.

question: In the chip shortage of around 2020-2021, why was automobile production heavily affected?
choices: Because cars use no semiconductors at all
Because procurement of automotive chips could not keep up with sudden shifts in demand, and a car cannot be completed if even one part is missing
Because car factories were converted into chip fabs
explanation: When the pandemic hit, automakers temporarily cut orders while work-from-home demand sent chip demand for PCs and similar products soaring; when car demand recovered, automotive chip supply could not keep up. Factory fires and cold-snap shutdowns compounded the problem. Since cars use many chips, a shortage of a single type of inexpensive microcontroller could halt production, prompting a rethink of lean procurement and supply chains.
choiceNotes: Cars use many semiconductors.
Correct. A shortage of even one part prevents completing a vehicle.
Car factories were not converted into chip fabs.

question: Which small computer, embedded in appliances, cars and other equipment to control them, integrates a CPU, memory and I/O circuits on one chip?
explanation: A microcontroller integrates a CPU, nonvolatile program memory, RAM, timers, A/D converters and other I/O on one chip, controlling everyday devices from rice cookers and air conditioners to car engines and brakes. A car carries dozens of microcontrollers, and luxury models more than a hundred. DRAM is for storage and an image sensor detects light.
choiceNotes: Correct. It is a small computer for controlling equipment.
DRAM is memory that stores data temporarily.
An image sensor converts light into electrical signals.

question: What is it called when large cloud providers and the like design their own chips specialized for AI processing and other tasks for their data centers and have them made by foundries?
explanation: Operators of large data centers increasingly design their own AI accelerators and CPUs optimized for their services, alone or with design partners, and have foundries manufacture them. Co-optimizing hardware with their own software aims to beat off-the-shelf products in performance and power efficiency and to reduce procurement costs. A second source means multiple suppliers, and the silicon cycle is the market's boom-bust cycle.
choiceNotes: Second sourcing means being able to procure equivalent parts from multiple suppliers.
The silicon cycle is the cycle of market booms and busts.
Correct. These are chips designed for the company's own uses.

question: Which law, enacted in the US in 2022, provides large subsidies and more for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and research and development?
explanation: The CHIPS and Science Act provided over 50 billion dollars, centered on manufacturing subsidies, to support semiconductor fab construction and R&D in the United States. In response, many companies are building new US fabs. Japan, Europe and South Korea have launched similar support programs. The RoHS directive and REACH regulation are EU rules on hazardous substances and chemicals.
choiceNotes: Correct. It is a law supporting the US semiconductor industry.
The RoHS Directive is the EU restriction on hazardous substances.
The REACH Regulation is the EU chemicals regulation.

question: Which Japanese company, founded in 2022, aims to mass-produce 2 nm-generation leading-edge logic chips in Chitose, Hokkaido?
explanation: Rapidus was founded in 2022 with investment from eight major Japanese companies, including Toyota and Sony Group, and large-scale government support, and is developing 2 nm logic in collaboration with IBM and others. It built a fab in Chitose, Hokkaido, started a pilot line in 2025, and aims to begin volume production around 2027. Kioxia is a leading NAND flash maker and Renesas a leading microcontroller maker.
choiceNotes: Kioxia is a major maker of NAND flash memory.
Correct. It is the company aiming for 2 nm-generation mass production.
Renesas is a major maker of microcontrollers and automotive chips.

question: Fabs place particular emphasis on keeping tool utilization high. Which is an appropriate reason?
choices: Because stopping tools makes the cleanroom dirty
Because high utilization makes tools last longer
Because fixed costs such as depreciation on huge investments in tools and buildings are large, so lower output sharply raises the cost per chip
explanation: Fab costs are dominated by fixed costs incurred regardless of output, such as depreciation of expensive equipment and buildings. When utilization drops, the same fixed costs are spread over fewer chips, raising cost per unit. Fabs therefore try to keep running even in downturns, sometimes by cutting prices, which can deepen price declines. Idling tools does not by itself contaminate the cleanroom.
choiceNotes: Stopping tools does not in itself make the cleanroom dirty.
Utilization and tool life are not the reason here.
Correct. It is because fixed costs make up a large share.

question: Which organization, made up of major semiconductor makers worldwide, publishes statistics and forecasts of semiconductor market shipments?
explanation: WSTS (World Semiconductor Trade Statistics) is an organization to which major chipmakers contribute shipment data; it compiles market-size statistics by product category and region and publishes market forecasts about twice a year. It is frequently cited for market size and growth figures. JEDEC is a standards body and ISO the International Organization for Standardization; neither publishes market statistics.
choiceNotes: Correct. It publishes semiconductor market statistics and forecasts.
JEDEC is an organization that sets semiconductor standards.
ISO is the International Organization for Standardization and does not publish market statistics.

question: Which international industry association, whose members include makers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment and materials, develops industry standards and holds the SEMICON exhibitions?
explanation: SEMI is an international industry association of companies in the equipment and materials supply chain for semiconductors, displays and more. It develops many SEMI standards covering wafer dimensions, carriers such as FOUPs, tool-to-factory communication and safety (such as SEMI S2), allowing tools from any vendor to work in the same fab. It also hosts SEMICON exhibitions worldwide. IEEE is a professional society and WSTS a statistics organization.
choiceNotes: WSTS is an organization that publishes semiconductor market statistics.
Correct. It is the industry association for manufacturing equipment and materials.
IEEE is a professional society for electrical and electronic engineering, not the organizer of SEMICON.

question: Which correctly describes chips made on so-called mature (legacy) processes older than the 28 nm generation?
choices: They are no longer used at all
They are used only in the latest smartphone CPUs
They are still used in huge volumes in microcontrollers, power devices, analog chips, sensors and the like, and are essential to cars and industrial equipment
explanation: Only some products, such as CPUs and GPUs, need leading-edge scaling; many microcontrollers, power-management ICs, analog chips, power devices and sensors are made on mature processes for reasons of cost, reliability and high-voltage capability. Mature processes run on depreciated equipment, making them cheap, and long-term supply is easier to commit to. They are used in vast quantities in cars, industrial equipment and appliances, and shortages of them became a problem during the chip crisis.
choiceNotes: Mature-process products are still used in huge volumes.
The latest smartphone CPUs are made on leading-edge processes.
Correct. They are an important product group supporting many kinds of equipment.

question: Which set correctly names major semiconductor manufacturing equipment makers?
choices: Applied Materials, ASML, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron and KLA
TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SMIC and GlobalFoundries
Qualcomm, NVIDIA, AMD, MediaTek and Broadcom
explanation: The equipment market is led by Applied Materials (US) in deposition and more, ASML (Netherlands) in lithography, Lam Research (US) in etch, Tokyo Electron (Japan) in coater/developers, deposition and cleaning, and KLA (US) in inspection and metrology. Japan also has many other globally strong equipment makers in areas such as cleaning, dicing, testers and mask inspection. TSMC and peers are chip manufacturers, and Qualcomm and peers are fabless companies.
choiceNotes: Correct. These are the major equipment makers.
These are chip manufacturers (foundries and IDMs).
These are fabless companies.

question: Which business model keeps fab investment down by making some products in its own fabs while outsourcing leading-edge products and the like to foundries?
explanation: Fab-lite companies make mature-process products and those where they have unique strengths in their own fabs, while outsourcing leading-edge products that require huge investment to foundries. Sitting between fabless (no fabs) and IDM (everything in-house), the model limits capital burden while preserving manufacturing know-how. It is common among major microcontroller, analog and power semiconductor makers. OSATs provide back-end services.
choiceNotes: Fabless means owning no manufacturing fabs.
Correct. It is a model that keeps fabs light.
An OSAT is a company that provides back-end services under contract.

question: Which correctly describes the book-to-bill (BB) ratio, used as an indicator of the semiconductor equipment market?
choices: Orders divided by shipments (billings); above 1 means orders exceed shipments, indicating strong demand
The proportion of good chips per wafer
The average interval between equipment failures
explanation: The book-to-bill ratio divides orders (bookings) by shipments (billings) over a period. Above 1, more orders are coming in than going out, signaling strong future demand; below 1, demand is weakening. For example, 12 billion yen in orders against 10 billion in shipments gives 1.2. North American equipment makers' figures were once published monthly and watched as a leading market indicator. It is unrelated to yield or MTBF.
choiceNotes: Correct. Demand strength is gauged from the ratio of orders to shipments.
That is yield.
That is MTBF.

question: In semiconductor and other manufacturing, what is the tendency called for the cost per unit to fall by a fixed percentage each time cumulative production doubles?
explanation: With the experience curve effect, unit cost falls as cumulative production grows, thanks to process improvements, higher yields and worker learning. It is often expressed as cost dropping 20–30% each time cumulative volume doubles. It is one reason early high-volume producers gain a cost advantage, and it underlay past DRAM capacity races. Moore's law and Dennard scaling are rules of thumb about technology progress.
choiceNotes: Dennard scaling describes the properties of proportionally shrinking transistors.
Moore's law is an empirical rule about the growth in transistor count.
Correct. It is the tendency for costs to fall with cumulative output.

question: For leading-edge logic chips, which is closest to the typical time from starting a wafer on the production line to completing the front-end process?
choices: Several months (roughly three months or more)
explanation: Leading-edge logic involves over a thousand steps of lithography, deposition, etching and more, so the front end alone takes three months or longer. Back-end assembly and testing add time, and building a new fab takes two years or more, so supply cannot respond quickly to demand spikes, one reason for mismatches and shortages. One day is far too short to complete so many steps, and ten years is far too long.
choiceNotes: Many steps cannot be completed in one day.
Correct. The front end alone takes several months.
It does not take as long as ten years.

question: What is it called when an equipment maker arranges to procure an equivalent product from another supplier as well, in case supply of a particular chip stops?
explanation: A second source means being able to procure parts of identical function and specification from multiple suppliers. If one supplier is halted by an accident, disaster or tight supply, production can continue, and it strengthens price negotiations. In the past, customers sometimes required second sources, leading chipmakers to license other companies to manufacture their designs. The recent chip shortages renewed its importance.
choiceNotes: Correct. It means securing multiple suppliers.
Tape-out is handing design data off to manufacturing.
A shrink is a remake of a chip at a smaller size.

question: When a chipmaker announces the end of life (EOL) of a product, what is it called when equipment makers using it buy, one last time, the quantity they will need for future maintenance and production?
explanation: When a chipmaker discontinues an old product, it accepts final orders for a set period. Makers of equipment needing ten or more years of supply and maintenance, such as automotive, industrial and medical equipment, use this chance to buy all the quantity they will need (a last-time buy) and store it long-term. Afterward they redesign around substitutes. An MPW is a prototyping service and just-in-time is a low-inventory philosophy.
choiceNotes: MPW is a scheme for prototyping multiple designs together on one wafer.
Just-in-time is the idea of procuring and producing only what is needed when it is needed.
Correct. It is the final bulk purchase before the end of production.

question: Which is the main reason the price per processed wafer has risen sharply as leading-edge process generations advance?
choices: Because the wafer diameter doubles every generation
Because the number of process steps and masks has grown and expensive tools such as EUV exposure systems are needed
Because silicon raw material is in short supply
explanation: Scaling requires more process steps and masks for multipatterning and complex transistor structures, along with extremely expensive tools such as EUV scanners. Wafer processing cost has therefore risen sharply, and the decline in cost per transistor has slowed compared with the past. Wafer diameter has stayed at 300 mm since around 2001, and a shortage of raw silicon is not the main reason.
choiceNotes: The wafer diameter remains 300 mm.
Correct. More complex processing and pricier tools are the main reasons.
A shortage of silicon raw material is not the main reason.
